acceptance_criteria: AC-1 For every tab of every tab strip in the shell, selecting that tab renders that tab's own panel, and a test asserts it tab by tab.
AC-2 A test asserts, for at least one screen, that a non-selected tab's panel is not rendered, so a component that renders every panel at once cannot pass.
AC-3 Administration's Project plan tab renders content taken from its own frame, in empty-database form; it is no longer blank.
AC-4 No two tabs on the same screen render the same panel text.
AC-5 The selected tab carries aria-selected, each panel carries role tabpanel associated with its tab, and keyboard arrow navigation changes the selection; a test asserts the keyboard path.
AC-6 The default route of every product screen still renders its empty state against an empty database, and the existing preview-fencing test passes unchanged.
AC-7 The frontend suite passes; its test count before and after is stated in SESSION_CLOSE.
AC-8 npm run build succeeds, including the TypeScript check it runs first.
AC-9 The repository privacy gate reports zero findings.
AC-10 No file outside ui2/frontend/ changed and no design frame changed.
AC-11 FIDELITY_NOTES.md records panels rather than strips and states plainly that the earlier claim was wrong.

baseline.authority: docs/design/UI2_0_B1_07_JOBS_SCREEN_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN) governs the Jobs surface, docs/design/UI2_0_B1_08_AUDIT_LOGS_SCREEN_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN) the audit and logs surface, and docs/design/UI2_0_B1_09_DEVICE_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN) the device workspace. docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_12.md (FROZEN) section 4 fixes the required first state: a clean empty database, the UI and its menus visible, nothing pre-populated. The design frames under docs/design/ui2_mockups/ are the fidelity reference.
baseline.observed_defect: Reported by the Product Owner against the merged shell and confirmed by direct interaction with the running application. ui2/frontend/src/shell/M3Widgets.tsx M3Tabs accepts only tabs: readonly string[] and renders a strip of labels with no panel of any kind. Every screen that uses it -- Operations with four tabs, Administration with four, Configuration with seven, and the Inventory detail pane with four -- then renders one fixed body underneath, unconnected to the selection. The Product Owner's words: you can walk the tabs and it is always the same screen, and Administration's Project plan tab shows nothing at all.
baseline.sequencing: Frontend only; independent of the deployment lane.
baseline.why_the_previous_pass_missed_it: FIDELITY_NOTES.md recorded the tab strips as matched. The strip does match the frame; the panels were never built. No test asserted that selecting a tab changes what is rendered, so a decorative strip passed a green suite.

invariants: A clean, empty database is the required first state; no panel is populated by default.
No credential, management address, device name or serial enters a tracked file.
No vendor data collection and no device contact: the standing collection gate holds.
The committed design frames stay in their scrubbed form and are never re-synced.
No HTTP surface gains a write capability in this movement.
No contract status is applied, removed or changed.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review of the diff, orchestrator verify.passed, and the Product Owner walking the tabs in the running application. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Make every tab strip in the shell a real tab control: selecting a tab changes the panel below it, each tab has its own panel with its own empty state written from its own design frame, and a test proves it for every tab of every screen.
output_contract: Tab strips that are real tab controls, with one distinct panel per tab across Operations, Administration, Configuration and the Inventory detail pane
Per-tab tests that fail if a panel is shared, missing, or all rendered at once
SESSION_CLOSE with the frontend test count before and after and the real output of every validation step

recommended_reasoning.reason: Nineteen panels across four screens, each needing its own empty state read from its own frame, plus a component contract change and per-tab tests. Volume and care rather than difficulty.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law
A tab that has nothing to show still gets a panel that says what is missing and why. An empty panel is a state, not an absence.
Every empty state must be specific to its own tab. Four tabs must not share one sentence.
The default route stays the empty state; the existing test fencing preview data out of product screens must keep passing unchanged.
Preview data stays fictional and obviously so; no literal that looks like a real address, hostname, serial or device name enters any file.
Do not weaken, skip or delete an existing test.
Publish SESSION_CLOSE with scripts/local_relay.py append using --report pointing at a JSON file you wrote first. Do not pass report JSON inline on the command line.
Do not open a pull request and do not merge. Commit on the lane and publish SESSION_CLOSE.
risks: Rendering every panel at once so the tests pass while the user still sees one long page; AC-2 exists to catch exactly this.
Writing one generic empty sentence and reusing it for every tab, which reproduces the defect in a new form.
Inventing content for a tab whose frame does not show any, rather than stating what is missing.
Breaking the preview fence while adding panels.
Copying a device-shaped literal out of a frame while transcribing panel copy.
